newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler shaves 8 months off LH car development.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler shaves 8 months off LH car development.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. developed its next-generation LH family of large cars eight months faster than it took the automaker to bring the current LH models to market in 1992, the cars' development chief said Monday.

John Miller, general manager of large car engineering for Chrysler, said he will tell an automotive conference here Tuesday that Chrysler's refined platform teams and advanced computer-aided design techniques shaved $75 million to $80 million off the LH cars' engineering costs.
Chrysler plans to launch production of two of the new LH cars -- the Dodge Intrepid and Chrysler Concorde -- in September. Two more, the LHS and 300M will debut next year.

The introduction marks the first time a car developed completely by Chrysler's super-efficient platform teams is being replaced. The automaker formed the teams in the late 1980s, when it was fighting for its life, in order to stretch its meagre resources and bring new products to market quickly.
"We've taken the whole concept of the platform team and evolved it over time," Miller said. "We've taken time out of the programme and cost out of the structure."

Chrysler is bringing the new LH cars to market at a total investment cost of $2.1 billion, compared to an initial $1.6 billion investment for the first LH, which was followed by additional costs to add capacity.
But for the new programme, Chrysler is gaining not only new cars, but three new aluminum V-6 engines, including a base 2.7-litre dual overhead camshaft engine and 3.2-litre and 3.5-litre powerplants.
Miller said the use of the CATIA design software by Chrysler and its suppliers allowed it to test thousands of parts in computer simulations before making costly prototypes.

During the engine design, he said engineers tested 1,500 potential intake manifold designs on computers before settling on the design that offered the best performance, fuel economy and noise performance.
As a result, the cars will come to market 31 months after their designs were approved, compared to 39 months for the current LH cars, which were introduced in the summer of 1992.

Miller said Chrysler's large car platform team is about the same size as it was in 1992 -- about 800 engineers, 1,000 people in total -- but it now also has responsibility for the company's JA mid-size car platform.

In addition to launching the Intrepid and Concorde, they also are developing the next generation Dodge Stratus, Chrysler Cirrus and Plymouth Breeze cars. The new JA cars are due in the 2000 model year, according to industry analysts.
